items.title: [AINews] How to steal a Reasoning Trace - Latent.Space
items.summary: Frontier Lab reasoning models' hidden reasoning can be extracted using a vulnerability in their APIs, allowing for the decoding of encrypted thought processes and potentially exposing personal data. Researchers found that 62 unique API keys, 33 email addresses, and 33 passwords were decoded from public traces. The technique involves replaying an encrypted reasoning block into a different request to a weaker model from the same provider, then transcribing the attached reasoning. This vulnerability has raised concerns about AI security and privacy.
items.audio_script:
From latent.space, "[AINews] How to steal a Reasoning Trace - Latent.Space". Researchers have discovered a vulnerability in Frontier Lab reasoning models' APIs that allows for the extraction of hidden reasoning traces, enabling the decoding of encrypted thought processes and potentially exposing personal data. The technique involves replaying an encrypted reasoning block into a different request to a weaker model from the same provider, then transcribing the attached reasoning. This process was tested using 62 unique API keys, 33 email addresses, and 33 passwords, which were successfully decoded from public traces. The researchers have highlighted this vulnerability as a concern for AI security and privacy, raising questions about the protection of sensitive information stored within these models.

The method employed to exploit this vulnerability relies on exploiting differences in how reasoning models process requests. By replaying an encrypted block into a different request, it is possible to take advantage of weaknesses in the API's design, effectively bypassing intended security measures. The successful decoding of sensitive data underscores the need for immediate attention and remediation from affected providers.

This vulnerability highlights a pressing concern for the AI industry, which must prioritize robust security protocols and safeguards to protect sensitive information stored within these models. As researchers continue to uncover vulnerabilities in AI systems, it is essential for developers and providers to implement necessary countermeasures to prevent similar breaches in the future.

items.summary:

items.title: Building and Validating a Quantitative Trading Strategy with OctoBot, Walk-Forward Backtesting, Parameter Optimization, and Interactive Analysis

items.title: Stop Calling the First Significant Day a Win
items.summary: Checking an A/B test until it crosses p < 0.05 can result in nearly 28 percent false-positive rate, compared to about 5 percent if checked only once at the end. The problem is that every new look gives the same random process another chance to wander across the line. If a team stops early on day four, for example, the pressure to stop becomes real, and the result can be overstated by up to a quarter. Using an always-valid p-value or group-sequential testing with calibrated boundaries can help mitigate this issue.
items.audio_script: From Towards Data Science, "Stop Calling the First Significant Day a Win", researchers have found that checking an A/B test until it crosses p < 0.05 can result in nearly 28 percent false-positive rate, compared to about 5 percent if checked only once at the end. Using an always-valid p-value or group-sequential testing with calibrated boundaries can help mitigate this problem. By adopting these methods, teams can minimize false positives and obtain more accurate results.

items.title: The Budget Split That Explains Itself
items.summary: Diversifying a budget without losing the shadow prices that explain the result requires careful consideration of diminishing returns. A mixed-integer program can be used instead of adding an on/off switch, where each channel's budget is sliced into bands with lower marginal yields. This approach allows the model to diversify without introducing binary decisions and retains the familiar LP shadow prices. By naming constraints and interpreting their values, users can uncover the costs associated with their safety rules and make more informed decisions.

items.title: Thinking of ACE? We Can Do It with Fewer Tokens
items.summary: A recent system, ALTK-Evolve, and ACE (Agentic Context Engineering) both use agentic memory to turn an agent's past trajectories into reusable lessons. However, they differ in delivery. ACE always sends all of the lessons on every step, regardless of model or task, while ALTK-Evolve sends only a small fixed core of high-support guidelines plus selectively retrieved guidelines for each task. This difference in delivery leads to variations in token usage: ACE uses significantly more tokens than ALTK-Evolve, but both systems achieve similar accuracy rates.
items.audio_script: From Hugging Face Blog, "Thinking of ACE? Researchers developed an alternative system called ALTK-Evolve, which uses agentic memory to turn an agent's past trajectories into reusable lessons. Unlike ACE, ALTK-Evolve sends only a small fixed core of high-support guidelines plus selectively retrieved guidelines for each task, leading to reduced token usage. The study demonstrates that this modified approach can be effective in achieving similar accuracy rates as ACE.

The tool was designed specifically for Pakistani judicial opinions and statutes, combining OpenAI's GPT-4 large language model with a knowledge base of nearly 130,000 judicial opinions and statutes. Training sessions for judges showed that those who received more comprehensive training logged in and used the tool persistently, resolving significantly more cases than those who received generic training.

items.title: Closed-Loop LLM Co-Pilots for Digital Agriculture
items.summary: Large Language Models (LLMs) are co-pilots in complex biological systems, analyzing data from a 49-channel phytosensor network to optimize plant physiology and trigger hardware actuators. The system provides real-time natural-language interpretation for both specialists and non-experts, enabling autonomous control of microclimates, phenotyping protocols, or stress scenarios. In a production-scale deployment, agents executed multi-parameter optimization, reducing the production cycle by 35% and energy consumption by 18%. The LLM autonomously developed an unforeseen strategy of dark-induced chlorophyll accumulation, resulting in a 67.9% energy saving.

items.title: SPOTting the Future: Lookahead Explanations for Deep Reinforcement Learning
items.summary: SPOT (Sampling Policy Observation Tree), a novel model-agnostic, sampling-based framework for interpreting deep reinforcement learning policies, constructs an interpretable finite-horizon tree by sampling actions and recursively simulating the resulting successor states. The tree provides an empirical representation of the policy's action preferences and their possible downstream evolution. SPOT achieves formal guarantees establishing its asymptotic recovery of the policy's unique most probable action, characterizing its disagreement behavior under high-entropy policies.

items.title: MIDAS: Mutual Information Disentanglement with Uncertainty-Aware Fusion for Incomplete Multimodal Sentiment Analysis
items.summary: Researchers propose a unified framework called Mutual Information Disentanglement with Uncertainty-Aware Fusion (MIDAS), which effectively restructures multimodal representations under incomplete conditions. MIDAS adopts a variational modeling strategy to represent each modality as a multivariate Gaussian latent variable and further decomposes them into shared and exclusive factors. An uncertainty-aware fusion mechanism is introduced, where posterior variance is leveraged as a reliability indicator to adaptively weight latent features during fusion, ensuring robust integration even when modalities are incomplete. Extensive experiments show that MIDAS achieves strong performance gains over competitive baselines across three widely used datasets.

items.title: Towards Sustainable Artificial Intelligence: A Comprehensive Review and Comparative Analysis of Deep Learning Models' Carbon Footprint
items.summary: Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Machine Learning (ML) have high energy demands and associated carbon emissions, primarily due to their high computational resources. This paper presents a systematic review of research on Green AI and Deep Learning (DL) models' carbon footprint, which highlights the training phase as the primary source of emissions. The results show that increased architectural complexity does not systematically translate into proportional accuracy gains, emphasizing the importance of balancing predictive performance and environmental cost.

items.title: ReCBM: Uncertainty-Gated Relational Reasoning for Concept Bottleneck Models
items.summary: ReCBM, an uncertainty-gated relational reasoning framework for Concept Bottleneck Models, introduces semantically defined concept relations into the bottleneck and uses uncertainty to guide their refinement. It models co-occurrence, implication, and exclusion to specify how evidence is exchanged across concepts, while uncertainty modulates the contribution of each concept during this process. Experiments showed that ReCBM improved concept and task recovery under missing and flipped concepts, supported uncertainty-aware intervention, and extracted compact task-relevant concept subsets without degrading downstream performance.

items.title: Automating and Scaling Behavioral Scientific Research on AI Agents
items.summary: Researchers developed AEROBAT, the first multi-agent system to automate behavioral scientific research on AI agents. It generates hypotheses, designs and executes controlled experiments, makes behavioral assessments, analyzes results, and writes reports. AEROBAT tested 79 hypotheses for 12 target behaviors, finding moderate-to-strong statistical evidence for 26 hypotheses, including novel ones. This demonstrates that automated behavioral scientific research can complement manual research and extend its reach.

items.title: CHORUS: Complementary Experts for High-Coverage Testbench Stimulus Generation
items.summary: CHORUS, a post-training framework, combines staged supervised fine-tuning (SFT) and dense-reward reinforcement learning (RL) to generate high-coverage testbench stimulus. The resulting specialists can be consolidated into a single model, achieving 88.0% Pass@1 on CVDP-ECov and outperforming DeepSeek-R1 by 13.5 percentage points.

items.title: MESA:Task-Adaptive Multi-Structure Evidence Selection for Long-Horizon Agent Memory
items.summary: MESA, a Multi-structure Evidence Selection framework for long-horizon Agent Memory, builds five complementary structure views of each trajectory and learns to select and fuse a query-specific subset using end-to-end answer-level feedback. MESA employs harness optimization with prior-guided search and UCB-guided scheduling to balance exploration and exploitation. On AMA-Bench, MESA outperforms the strongest baseline by 8.5% while using 41% fewer evidence tokens than the all-structure alternative.

items.title: The CASE Framework: A Multi-Disciplinary Control Architecture for Governing Enterprise Agentic AI
items.summary: The CASE Framework proposes a multi-disciplinary control architecture for governing enterprise agentic AI, assigning Control theory to individual agents, complex Adaptive systems theory to collective agent behavior, Supervisory cybernetics to human-agent teams, and Engineering operations to fleets. The framework identifies the Emergence Gap, where excellence at one layer strains others, and proposes a five-level maturity model with assessment instrument operationalizing CASE as a scientific rather than process maturity model. This gap becomes increasingly critical as EU AI Act Article 14 makes effective human oversight a legal requirement for enterprises deploying agentic AI.

items.title: SBCO: Self-Supervised, Verifier-Grounded Harness Optimization For Planning Agents
items.summary: SBCO (Self-supervised Block Coordinate Optimizer) is a verifier-grounded harness optimizer that improves planning agents through self-supervised learning with approximate block coordinate ascent, learning a decomposed bank of verifiers and a harness policy. SBCO matches or exceeds customized self-modifying baselines while using 4-5.5 times less compute budget across two domains. It operates in a closed-loop, improve-from-experience framework with a fixed meta-agent and no human labels.

items.title: Transformer Geometry Observatory TGO-IV: Developmental Topology Observatory
items.summary: Researchers have developed Transformer Geometry Observatory TGO-IV, a topological framework to analyze the evolution of transformer representations using persistent homology. This framework constructs Vietoris-Rips simplicial complexes from token-level representation point clouds and investigates their persistent topological signatures across transformer layers. It uses various metrics, including Persistence Diagrams, Barcode Diagrams, Betti Curves, Persistence Landscapes, Bottleneck Distance, and Wasserstein Distance, to study the global topology of representation point clouds throughout the forward pass.

items.title: Uncertainty-Aware Ensemble Deep Randomized Neural Networks for Classification
items.summary: Researchers proposed intuitionistic fuzzy dRVFL and IF-edRVFL frameworks to enhance model robustness in deep randomized neural networks, which can handle real-world datasets containing noise and outliers. The models assign adaptive weights to training samples based on membership and non-membership degrees computed from the distance of samples from class centroids. Extensive experiments on UCI and KEEL benchmark datasets demonstrate superiority over existing fuzzy and non-fuzzy approaches.

items.title: CurveFP: Rational-Radix Logarithmic Datatypes with Closed Products for Language Models
items.summary: CurveFP is a closed-product codebook family designed to reduce language-model cost by distributing quantized magnitudes across interleaved logarithmic curves under compact block scales. A rational radix tunes dynamic range against local resolution, while uniform curve indices make every nonzero product algebraically closed. CurveFP eight and seven demonstrate improved numerical behavior and reduced format-induced penalties compared to FP8 in various evaluations.

items.title: Sheaf-Based Federated Representation Learning
items.summary: Sheaf-based Federated Representation Learning (SFRL) proposes a general framework to jointly optimize local objectives with a manifold-constrained geometric alignment regularizer based on learnable sheaf restriction maps. SFRL does not assume a shared global latent space, instead relying on orthogonal transformations and isometric embeddings for global consistency. The alignment of neighboring latent representations is enforced by a quadratic gluing regularizer induced by the sheaf Laplacian.

items.title: DOCSCHISEL: Adaptive Tool Documentation Optimization Framework for LLM Agents
items.summary: DOCSCHISEL, an adaptive tool documentation optimization framework, was proposed to address the critical issue of ground resource for LLM agents. The study revealed substantial heterogeneity in tool documentation and found that its effectiveness depends on task domain, LLM backbone, and agent paradigm. DocsChisel analyzes failed execution traces to identify documentation-related issues and optimizes tool documentation by adding, removing, and refining information fields. Experimental results show a 95.89% improvement in task success rate over original tool documentation and a 75.15% average improvement over existing baselines.

items.title: FlowScout: From Execution Feedback to Reliable Tool-Using Agent Workflows
items.summary: FlowScout proposes an execution-guided framework for generating agentic workflows from historical task-solving records, representing a workflow as a directed graph composed of LLM nodes, tool-calling nodes, and dependency edges. It first mines a common tool coordination skeleton and then refines the workflow topology through Monte Carlo tree search guided by execution feedback, achieving significant improvements in tool invocation correctness and execution quality over baselines.

items.title: UserToolBench: A User-Profile-Hidden Benchmark for Personalized Decision Making in Tool-Use LLMs
items.summary: UserToolBench is a benchmark for personalized decision making in tool-use LLMs. It tests whether a model can infer latent user preferences, recognize clarification needs, and produce user-aligned tool-call trajectories under incomplete information. The benchmark includes 10 user profiles, 36 tool sets, and evaluation-focused task types covering lack-of-information, single-tool, and multi-tool settings. Experiments show that current models struggle with personalized delegation, particularly in multi-tool coordination, missing-constraint inference, and long-horizon behavioral consistency.

items.title: Finding the Signal in the Spam: Jointly Learning Rewards and Worker Reliability from Pairwise Comparisons
items.summary: Researchers developed an algorithm to learn item rewards and worker reliability jointly from pairwise comparisons, reducing the impact of unreliable workers in crowdsourcing settings. The algorithm uses a Boltzmann-rational model that incorporates worker competencies and introduces Polya-Gamma latent variables for tractable optimization. The method demonstrates strong robustness to spammers and adversarial workers, achieving advantages over several baselines in experiments on real-world and synthetic datasets.

items.title: Detecting Soft Skills in ML Engineering Roles CVs
items.summary: CVs for machine learning (ML) engineering roles reveal that candidates disclose soft skills through narrative rather than keyword lists by a ratio of 3:1, with leadership, coordination, and mentoring being the most commonly articulated competencies. Seniority nearly triples the odds of articulating leadership, but software engineers articulate this competency at half the rate of their peers.

items.title: Physics-Informed Machine Learning in Prognostics and Health Management: A Systematic Literature Review
items.summary: A systematic literature review of 212 studies on Physics-Informed Machine Learning (PIML) in Prognostics and Health Management (PHM) demonstrates improved predictive performance over conventional baselines across a broad range of assets. The reviewed studies are heavily skewed toward lithium-ion batteries and bearings, with problem-specific solutions. While PIML approaches provide tangible benefits, claims of improvements concerning some limitations lack sufficient supporting evidence. Future research should prioritize transferable design patterns, benchmarks comparing integration strategies, and uncertainty-aware models for online deployment in real-world settings.

items.title: Deciding When to Switch: E-Processes for Adaptive Minimax Training for Generative Adversarial Nets
items.summary: Researchers Hyunjoo Kim and colleagues propose an e-process-based adaptive training procedure for Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs), which enables decisions about when to switch between discriminator and generator updates. The method tests hypotheses during training, ensuring anytime-valid Type I error control under adaptive model updates and data-dependent switching. It outperforms fixed-ratio baselines on multimodal synthetic distributions and image benchmark datasets across several GAN objectives.

items.title: Iterative Erasure Count Is Not an Affine-Invariant Concept Dimension
items.summary:
Iterative Erasure Count Is Not an Affine-Invariant Concept Dimension. 

The iterative erasure count, a common measure of concept dimension, is not affine-invariant. It changes under information-preserving invertible reparameterization, such as shear transformations. In contrast, the cumulative edit rank and sufficient linear dimension are also affected by reparameterization. However, the complete cumulative metric-QR trajectory remains affine-equivariant when certain parameters are consistently transported.

items.title: Spectral Embeddings of Degree-$\alpha$ Laplacians in Random Dot Product Graphs
items.summary: Researchers John Park and Ning Hao established a row-wise central limit theorem for spectral embeddings of degree-$\alpha$ Laplacians in random dot product graphs. The result provides explicit descriptions of how degree normalization affects population geometry and local uncertainty of embedded nodes, depending on network density, community imbalance, and block-probability structure.

items.title: Self-Normalized Inference for Constant-Stepsize Temporal-Difference Learning under Markovian Sampling
items.summary: Researchers Min Zeng, Yichen Zhang, and Xiaofeng Shao developed a method for inference in constant-stepsize temporal-difference learning under Markovian sampling. They established a functional central limit theorem and derived a joint functional limit for parallel Richardson-Romberg recursions, enabling asymptotically pivotal confidence regions without estimating covariance or selecting a bandwidth or batch length. The procedure admits a one-pass implementation with no growing memory.

items.title: Conditional Independence Tests for Constraint-Based Causal Discovery: A Survey
items.summary: Conditional Independence (CI) tests in constraint-based causal discovery rely on statistical engines such as PC and FCI, which use skeleton pruning and key orientations based on CI decisions. The survey categorizes widely used CI methods into six families: partial-correlation, contingency-table, regression, nearest-neighbor, kernel, and machine-learning-based. It also examines the robustness of these families, comparing test-level properties to graph-level errors in skeleton recovery and v-structure orientation.

items.title: Optimized Sequential Testing for Binary Ensemble Classifiers
items.summary: Researchers Joseph Kalman and Amit Moscovich propose an optimized sequential testing approach to reduce the computational cost of binary ensemble classifiers. By evaluating base models sequentially, they can stop execution when a clear majority emerges, providing significant speed-ups (up to 4x) while controlling disagreement at 0.1%. The optimal stopping strategy is found using linear programs.

items.title: Optimal Inference with Black-box Predictions
items.summary: Researchers Lucas Kania and colleagues developed practical hypothesis tests that adapt to the unknown accuracies of black-box predictions while benefiting from strong alignment among them, addressing the gap in statistical inference. They characterized information-theoretic limits of inference with known and unknown prediction accuracies. The work aims to provide a unifying principle for combining observed data with predictions in a valid and efficient way.

items.title: The sharp SAT/UNSAT phase transition in random ellipsoid fitting
items.summary: Saunderson, Parrilo and Willsky conjectured that as n,d approach infinity, a semidefinite feasibility problem undergoes a sharp transition at n ≈ d^2/4. The authors prove this conjecture: if lim sup n/d^2 = α* < 1/4, an ellipsoid fit exists with probability tending to one and all eigenvalues in a fixed interval.

items.title: COMPACT: Spectral Adjustment Scores from a Complete and Irreducible Causal Criterion
items.summary: Researchers Eric V. Strobl and colleagues have developed the COMPACT (Complete and Irreducible Causal Criterion for Treatments) method, which generates spectral adjustment scores from a complete causal criterion. This approach aims to maximize specificity over causal graphs by identifying unconditional and conditional dependence relations that are invariant to treatment effects. The method uses a generalized eigenvalue problem to operationalize the criterion and provides bootstrap validity through simulations and real-data applications.

items.title: Improved cross-validated distances for multivariate pattern analysis
items.summary: Laurent Caplette and Sarah Lippé have improved upon recommended distances for multivariate pattern analysis. They demonstrate that the cross-validated Euclidean distance can be equivalent to a sum of between-partition distances, leading to a generalized variant with increased reliability and accuracy. Additionally, they define a cross-validated correlation distance using the relationship between Euclidean distance and Pearson correlation, resulting in a more accurate and interpretable measure.
